title: StaR: Stateful Dynamic-Graph Root Cause Analysis through Memory-Enhanced Causality Discovery

problem.claim: Root-cause identification for anomalies in complex multivariate time-series systems is important for service reliability.

gap.claim: Existing causal-discovery approaches largely assume static causal relationships and process data without persistent state, limiting their ability to model dynamic topologies and stateful failure patterns.

contributions.claim: StaR is a stateful root-cause-analysis framework that reformulates Granger causal discovery using Temporal Graph Networks as the predictive engine.
StaR introduces persistent memory states and dynamic message passing into causal inference to model evolving graph structures and long-term dependencies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on nine datasets reportedly show that StaR consistently outperforms baselines.
The reported AC@1 improvement ranges from 0.028 to 0.920 on dynamic and stateful datasets.
On real-world datasets, the reported AC@1 improvement ranges from 0.381 to 0.752.

narrative_sequence.summary: Root-cause analysis is needed to maintain reliability in complex multivariate time-series systems.
Existing causal-discovery methods are limited by static relationship assumptions and stateless processing.
StaR addresses the limitations by combining Granger causal discovery with Temporal Graph Networks.
Persistent memory states and dynamic message passing represent evolving graph structures and long-term dependencies.
The authors report gains over baselines across nine datasets, including dynamic, stateful, and real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that static and memoryless models fail to capture dynamic topologies and stateful failure patterns.

interpretation.claim: Systems with evolving structure and long-lived failure effects may require models that jointly represent topology changes and persistent state.

application.claim: For root-cause analysis in changing systems, consider combining dynamic graph modeling with memory mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets or system settings.

unknowns: The nine dataset identities and their characteristics are not specified.
Baseline identities, experimental protocol, and statistical details are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the implementation or training details of the Temporal Graph Network and memory mechanisms.
